statements.t: Our integrated solutions are designed to streamline project execution, increase energy yield and long-term reliability, and enhance customer return on investment.
We have shipped more than 160 GW of solar tracker systems as of October 2, 2026 to projects on six continents for use in utility-scale and distributed generation solar applications.
Our customers include engineering, procurement and construction firms (“EPCs”), as well as solar project developers and owners.
For the majority of our projects, our direct customer is the EPC.
We also engage with project owners and developers and enter into master supply agreements that cover multiple projects.
We are a qualified, preferred provider to some of the largest solar EPCs, project owners and developers in the world.

Further, the acquisition from Zigor/Apex expands our energy infrastructure technology portfolio, including UL-certified central inverters for utility-scale solar and energy storage projects in the United States.
We have expanded our sales organization and expect to scale our sales headcount to support our planned growth.

We have incurred and expect to continue to incur on an ongoing basis certain new costs related to the requirements of being a publicly traded company, including insurance, accounting, tax, legal and other professional services costs, which could be material.
We expect that the dollar amount of research and development expenses will increase in amount over time.
We expect to receive a tax benefit for foreign tax credits in the United States for the foreign tax paid.

Revenue increased approximately $393.8 million, or 31% in the U.S. during the six-month period ended October 2, 2026 compared to the six-month period ended September 26, 2025 as the number of projects and volume of shipments increased year over year in addition to the additional revenue from our acquisitions and the Rest of the World decreased $118.9 million, or 25%, primarily from decreased shipments to Latin…

estimates.t: The preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“U.S.

estimates.name: Key components of our results of operations
estimates.t: The following discussion describes certain line items in our unaudited condensed consolidated statements of operations.

estimates.name: Revenue
estimates.t: We derive our revenue primarily from the sale of solar trackers and energy yield management systems to our customers.

estimates.name: Cost of sales and gross profit
estimates.t: Cost of sales consists primarily of purchased components net of any incentives or rebates earned from our suppliers, shipping and other logistics costs, applicable tariffs, standard product warranty costs, amortization of certain acquired intangible assets, stock-based compensation and direct labor.

estimates.name: Operating expenses — Selling, general and administrative expenses
estimates.t: Selling, general and administrative expenses consist primarily of personnel-related costs associated with our administrative and support functions.

estimates.name: Research and development
estimates.t: Research and development expenses consist primarily of personnel-related costs associated with our engineering employees, stock-based compensation, third-party consulting and supporting our new business acquisitions.

estimates.name: Income tax expense
estimates.t: The provision for income taxes primarily represents the Company’s U.S. federal, state, and local income taxes as well as foreign income taxes payable by its subsidiaries.
